summary: Three distribution lists for sending out Network documents such as RFCs, for sites, the NIC and station agents. These were postal addresses, not email lists. It replaced RFC 300 and was replaced by RFC 329.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 303 defines three lists of people and organizations that should receive ARPA Network documents. It separates initial recipients from non-site participants and local station agents.

subtitle: Three distribution lists for ARPA Network documents and their recipients.

tldr.problem: The ARPA Network needed defined recipient lists for distributing network documents from sites and from the Network Information Center.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines lists for initial distribution, NIC distribution to non-site participants, and NIC distribution to station agents.
tldr.outcome: RFC 303 obsoleted RFC 300 and was later obsoleted by RFC 329.

facts.label: Station Agent mailing frequency
facts.value: Once a week, or more often when quantity warrants

today: RFC 303 is an early ARPA Network document-distribution directory. It was later obsoleted by RFC 329.

sections.title: Three Document Distribution Lists
sections.content:
The RFC provides three lists for distributing Network documents. Sites use List A to send their documents to liaisons quickly, and the Network Information Center (NIC) uses Lists B and C to distribute copies to non-site Network Participants and Station Agents.

The document says phone numbers and lists of names by site are in the Current Directory of Network Participants. It obsoletes RFC 300.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo organizes recipients into three lists. Sites use one for liaisons, while the NIC uses the others for participants outside sites and for local station agents.

sections.title: What Each List Is For
sections.content:
List A is the initial distribution list. It includes Network Liaisons and others who should receive initial RFC distribution, whether sent by the NIC or by sites, along with selected catalogs and formal documents from the NIC.

List B covers NIC distribution to non-site Network Participants. List C contains NIC Station Agents, who receive copies of documents sent to liaisons and station collections. The NIC sends to Station Agents once a week, or more often when the quantity warrants.
sections.plainLanguage: List A is for initial recipients. List B is for participants outside network sites, and List C is for station agents who receive and handle documents locally.

sections.title: How the Lists Were Used
sections.content:
The document gives names and mailing addresses for the contacts on the lists. It instructs sites to send RFCs to liaisons as quickly as possible and says all mail other than local mail should be sent by air mail.

The lists are recipient directories, not protocol definitions. They identify who should receive documents and which organization is responsible for the distribution.
sections.plainLanguage: The lists identify people and mailing addresses for document delivery. They describe distribution responsibilities rather than a network protocol.
